parts.text: Copper( II ) sulfate is heated strongly. The products are copper( II ) oxide and sulfur trioxide. heat CuSO 4 → CuO + SO 3

parts.label: i
parts.text: (a) (i) What type of reaction is this? Tick one box. addition neutralisation oxidation thermal decomposition [1]

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Sulfur trioxide is an acidic gas. What precautions must be taken when heating copper( II ) sulfate in the laboratory? ....................................................................................................................................... [1]

ms.label: 3(a)(ii)
ms.text: use fume cupboard / fume hood / well-ventilated area;

ms.label: 3(a)(iii)

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) Sulfur trioxide dissolves in water to form sulfuric acid.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Complete the symbol equation for this reaction. SO 3 + H 2 O → ..................... [1]

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Sulfuric acid is strongly acidic. Which one of the following pH values is strongly acidic? Put a ring around the correct answer. pH 1 pH 6 pH 7 pH 9 pH 13 [1]

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) Copper( II ) oxide is a solid. An aqueous solution of copper( II ) sulfate can be made by heating excess copper( II ) oxide with dilute sulfuric acid. Draw a labelled diagram of the apparatus you would use to separate the excess copper( II ) oxide from the solution. [2]

ms.label: 3(c)
ms.text:
filter funnel and filter paper;
either funnel or filter paper labelled;

parts.label: d
parts.text: (d) Anhydrous copper( II ) sulfate can be used to test for water. CuSO 4 (s) + 5H 2 O(l) CuSO 4 .5H 2 O(s)
